answer: A sport I have always wanted to try is scuba diving, which has fascinated me for as long as I can remember. The idea of exploring the underwater world, with its vibrant coral and marine life, is genuinely [[captivating]]. Growing up beside the Jamuna, I spent a lot of time in and around water, but I have only seen the sea a couple of times, at Cox's Bazar. I want to try it because I love the ocean and I am drawn to the sense of adventure it offers. I would most like to do it at Saint Martin's Island, which is the only coral island in Bangladesh. To prepare, I would need to take a proper certified course, since safety is [[paramount]] in an activity like this. I can swim, as I learned in my grandparents' village pond as a boy, but I would need to build up my stamina and get used to breathing through the equipment. I imagine my first dive would be both terrifying and [[exhilarating]] in equal measure. I have watched countless videos of divers gliding past shoals of fish, and I always find myself wishing I were there. There is something about entering a completely different environment that appeals to my sense of curiosity. Honestly, I think it would be an [[unforgettable]] experience, quite unlike anything I have done before. Of course, it requires overcoming a certain amount of fear, but I think that is part of the appeal. It is firmly on my list of things to do, and I am [[resolved]] to try it one day.

followUps.q: Would you go diving alone or with friends?
followUps.answer: Definitely with friends, and of course with a qualified instructor. Sharing something that nerve-racking with people you know makes it less frightening, and it gives you a story to laugh about together afterwards.

followUps.q: Is scuba diving popular in your country?
followUps.answer: Not really, although it is slowly growing. Most people here see the sea as somewhere to walk along the beach, so diving is still a fairly [[niche]] activity, mainly for adventurous young people.
